observation.visible_scene: A thick stack of white paper sits on the round black grate of an outdoor charcoal grill, with green grass visible around the rim. The front-facing edge of the stack is already burned: it curls upward into dark, flaky black ash with brown scorched margins, while the upper and rear sheets remain flat and white. A thin black wire/cord loops across the right side of the stack, and glowing embers are visible in the grate below. Orange flames and grey smoke appear intermittently at the right edge and top corner of the paper.
visible_changes: The burning is already underway at the first frame; the charred, curling front edge keeps roughly the same shape and extent throughout the excerpt rather than visibly advancing.
Orange flames flicker on the right side of the stack, rising and falling in height and intensity from frame to frame (e.g., small at t=0.0, taller at t=0.467, t=0.667, t=1.8, t=2.467).
Brief flame tongues also appear along the top edge of the paper at several moments (e.g., t=0.2, t=0.467, t=0.667, t=2.467, t=2.667).
Thin grey smoke wisps drift upward, mainly from the left side and around the burning edges, with their position and density changing frame to frame.
The white unburned portion of the top sheet and the overall stack outline stay essentially fixed in place relative to the grill; no translation or collapse of the stack is observed.

The framing drifts slightly: the grill handle on the left and the grass background shift position and the view appears to slowly zoom/pan, indicating minor camera movement rather than motion of the paper.
outside_clip_unknowns: What initially ignited the paper and the embers beneath is not shown.
Whether the fire eventually consumes the whole stack or is extinguished is beyond this segment.
The exact material of the wire/cord draped on the right is not identifiable.
uncertain_details: The small change in framing could be a slow camera pan/zoom or a slight repositioning of the grill; background evidence is limited, so camera motion is treated as uncertain.
The apparent size/shape changes of the flames are flicker of an ongoing fire, not new ignition events.
The charred edge's constant appearance suggests a steady burning front, but no measurable progression is clearly visible within this short excerpt.
